input.quote: Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
input.rationale: Section 17 addresses only Sparkling's obligations to stop using and return Garman's Software, Documentation and Codes; there is no reciprocal obligation on Garman to provide transition assistance, return Sparkling's data (converted and hosted under Section 4/Schedule D) in a usable format, or certify deletion. The only data-return language is in Section 8, which applies solely if Sparkling rejects the Software during acceptance, and the escrow in Section 16 is at most a partial substitute. We therefore insert a new Section 17(d) with six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, a 30-day machine-readable data return and post-return deletion certification, and add it to the Section 18 survival list so it operates after termination.

proposal.summary: Insert Section 17(d) requiring Garman to provide transition assistance and return/delete Sparkling's data on termination, and add it to the survival list.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a transition and data-return provision at Section 17(d) so that, on any expiry or termination, Garman gives us up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates and returns our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days before certifying deletion; the agreement currently addresses return of Garman's Software but says nothing about our own data or an orderly exit. If six months is an issue we can accept ninety days of assistance, provided the thirty-day data export remains.

ops.text: (d) Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Garman shall (1) at Sparkling's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Garman's then-current rates; (2) within thirty (30) calendar days of Sparkling's request, return to Sparkling all of Sparkling's data in its possession or control in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (3) thereafter delete Sparkling's data from its systems and certify such deletion to Sparkling in writing.
